requirement: Training, validation and testing data sets meet the quality criteria of paragraphs 2 to 4 and Art. 4a(1) whenever used. Where no model training is involved, the criteria apply to testing data only.
proposed_control: Inventory of data sets per high-risk system, stating their use (training, validation, testing).
expected_evidence: Data set register linked to the use-case register.
notes: Anchor row for the article; the following rows break down paragraph 2.

requirement: Data governance and management practices appropriate to the intended purpose, covering design choices and the formulation of assumptions about what the data measure and represent.
proposed_control: Data governance procedure with mandatory fields for design choices and assumptions.
sme_variant: One-page data governance sheet per system instead of a formal procedure.
expected_evidence: Approved procedure; record of design decisions per system.

requirement: Data collection processes and origin of data and, for personal data, the original purpose of collection.
iso27701: A.1: purpose identification; legal basis; records of PII processing
proposed_control: Provenance record per data set: origin, licence or terms, legal basis and original purpose; compatibility test when data are reused.
expected_evidence: Provenance sheet; compatibility test (Art. 6(4) GDPR); data supplier contracts.
notes: Direct crossing point with the GDPR: the single intake form should capture the original purpose.

requirement: Data preparation operations: annotation, labelling, cleaning, updating, enrichment and aggregation.
proposed_control: Versioned labelling instructions; annotation quality control (sampling and inter-annotator agreement).
expected_evidence: Labelling instructions; annotation QA reports; data version history.

requirement: Assessment of the availability, quantity and suitability of the data sets needed.
proposed_control: Documented data sufficiency assessment before training, with acceptance criteria.

requirement: Examination of possible biases likely to affect health and safety, fundamental rights or lead to prohibited discrimination, especially where outputs feed future inputs (feedback loops).
proposed_control: Define intended behaviour and relevant groups; test performance metrics per group; identify feedback loops.
expected_evidence: Bias test plan; results per group; feedback-loop analysis.

requirement: Appropriate measures to detect, prevent and mitigate identified biases.
proposed_control: Mitigation plan with owner and thresholds; human review when a threshold is exceeded; re-test after every change.

requirement: Identification of data gaps or shortcomings that prevent compliance, and how they can be addressed.
proposed_control: Data gap register with a decision (fix, accept, restrict purpose).

requirement: Data sets are relevant, sufficiently representative and, to the best extent possible, free of errors and complete, with appropriate statistical properties for the persons or groups concerned.
proposed_control: Data quality metrics (completeness, errors, representativeness) with thresholds per system.
sme_variant: Documented sample check instead of automated metrics.
expected_evidence: Data quality report per data set version.
notes: The tension with GDPR minimisation is resolved through purpose: document why each attribute is needed.

requirement: Data sets take into account the characteristics of the geographical, contextual, behavioural or functional setting in which the system is intended to be used.
proposed_control: Describe the context of use at intake and validate data coverage against it.

requirement: Exceptional processing of special categories of personal data to detect and correct bias, only if all conditions are met: not achievable with synthetic or anonymised data; technical limits on reuse and pseudonymisation; access controls and access documentation; no transfer to third parties; deletion once bias is corrected or retention ends; reasons recorded in the record of processing activities.
ai_act_basis: Art. 4a(1)(a) to (f) (introduced by the AI Omnibus; replaces former Art. 10(5))
application_date: Chapter I: applicable (Omnibus recital 9; Art. 113 unchanged for Chapter I)
iso27701: A.1: legal basis; A.3: pseudonymisation; access control; PII de-identification and deletion
proposed_control: Prior authorisation procedure with a checklist of the six conditions; isolated environment; pseudonymisation; access log; scheduled deletion.
expected_evidence: Signed checklist; justification in the RoPA; access logs; proof of deletion.
notes: A legal basis, not an obligation. Without all six conditions, this basis does not apply.

requirement: Deployers of high-risk systems, and providers and deployers of other AI systems and models, may process special categories of data to detect and correct bias where strictly necessary and under the conditions of paragraph 1. Creates no obligation to do so.
iso27701: A.1: legal basis; A.3: access control; deletion
proposed_control: Same procedure as R-10.11, also available for systems outside high-risk.
notes: AI Omnibus novelty relevant to deployers: extends the legal basis beyond high-risk systems.

requirement: Technical documentation with data sheets: training methodologies, description of data sets, provenance, scope, characteristics, how data were obtained and selected, labelling and cleaning.
proposed_control: Data sheet template fed by the records from rows R-10.02 to R-10.09.
expected_evidence: Data sheet per data set, attached to the technical documentation.
notes: SMEs and small mid-caps may use the Commission's simplified form (Art. 11(1)).

requirement: Poisoning of training data or retrieval sources (RAG) that alters system behaviour.
proposed_control: Data provenance and integrity (hashes); source validation; adversarial testing; separation between untrusted data and instructions.
notes: Confirmed in the text: Art. 15(5) names data poisoning and model poisoning.

requirement: Reuse of client or employee data for training or fine-tuning, by us or by the vendor, without a legal basis or against contractual terms.
iso27701: A.1: purpose limitation; A.2: processing only on customer instructions; no use for other purposes
proposed_control: Data classification by system type; contractual no-training clause; vendor assessment; DLP on AI channels.
expected_evidence: Reviewed vendor terms; vendor assessment; approved classification rule.
notes: Ties into an existing programme: approved tool list and vendor assessments.

requirement: The high-risk system technically allows automatic recording of events (logs) over its lifetime.
proposed_control: Logging requirement in the system specification; logging on by default and not switchable off by the user.
expected_evidence: Specification; acceptance test demonstrating log generation.
notes: Design obligation of the provider. The deployer retains and uses the logs (R-12.07, R-12.08).

requirement: Logs allow identifying situations that may result in the system presenting a risk within the meaning of Art. 79(1) or in a substantial modification.
proposed_control: Event catalogue: model and prompt version, configuration changes, failures, safeguard activations, performance drift.

requirement: Logs facilitate post-market monitoring.
standards: prEN 18229-1; EN 18286:2026 (post-market monitoring within the QMS)
standard_status: Draft (prEN) / harmonised standard cited in the OJ
proposed_control: Monitoring dashboard fed by the logs; alert thresholds linked to the post-market plan.
to_confirm: Annex ZA coverage of EN 18286 regarding Art. 72.
notes: EN 18286 is the only standard in this matrix carrying a presumption of conformity, and only for high-risk providers and only for what it covers.

requirement: Logs allow the deployer to monitor the operation of the system.
proposed_control: Log export to the deployer and instructions for use on how to interpret them.

requirement: Remote biometric identification (Annex III, point 1(a)): minimum logging of each period of use, reference database, matched input data and identity of the persons who verified the results.
proposed_control: Applicable only if such a system exists. Otherwise mark not applicable with reasons.

requirement: The provider keeps the logs under its control for a period appropriate to the intended purpose, at least six months, unless other law provides otherwise (in particular data protection law). Financial institutions keep them as part of the documentation required by financial services law.
iso27701: A.3: retention and disposal of PII
proposed_control: Log retention policy per system, with a six-month minimum and deletion after the period.
to_confirm: Sectoral or national retention periods that prevail.

requirement: The deployer keeps the logs under its control for an appropriate period, at least six months.
iso27701: A.3: retention and disposal of PII
proposed_control: Define for each deployed system where the logs live, who controls access and for how long.
sme_variant: Periodic export of vendor logs to own storage, with a six-month period.
expected_evidence: Retention policy; contract with the provider where the logs sit on their side.
implemented_control: 12-month retention in the SIEM; AI log retention policy (example — replace)
to_confirm: Where the logs sit with the vendor, the obligation covers only logs under our control: confirm access contractually.

requirement: The deployer monitors operation based on the instructions; suspends use and informs the provider or distributor and the authority where there is a risk within the meaning of Art. 79(1); reports serious incidents.
proposed_control: Monitoring and escalation procedure, with suspension criteria and provider and authority contacts.
notes: One incident may trigger the AI Act (Art. 73) and the GDPR (Arts. 33 and 34) at the same time.

requirement: Logs contain personal data: minimisation, access control, security and a retention period consistent with the purpose.
iso27701: A.1: data minimisation; A.3: pseudonymisation; logging of PII access
proposed_control: Pseudonymise identifiers in logs; separate prompt content from metadata; dedicated access profile.
expected_evidence: Log design approved by the DPO; RoPA entry.
notes: Reconciles AI Act traceability with GDPR minimisation.

requirement: Logs insufficient to reconstruct what an agent did: tool calls, retrieved data, human approvals, model and prompt versions.
proposed_control: Structured log per agent action, with user identity carried through, human gate recorded and integrity protected (append-only, hashes).
notes: Where an existing programme already has controls (human gates, retry limits).

requirement: Tampering with or loss of logs that removes their evidential value.
proposed_control: Immutable storage, backups, clock synchronisation, write access only for the system.

requirement: Risk management system established, implemented, documented and maintained as a continuous iterative process throughout the lifecycle, with regular systematic review and updating.
standards: prEN 18228 (risk management); ISO/IEC 23894; ISO 9001:2015 clause 6.1 (actions to address risks and opportunities)
guidance: NIST AI RMF 1.0 — Govern and Map
proposed_control: AI risk management procedure integrated into the existing management system, with a review cadence per system and per change.
sme_variant: One-page procedure within general risk management, reviewed yearly and on relevant change.
expected_evidence: Approved procedure; risk register per system; review minutes.
notes: May be integrated into risk procedures required by sectoral law (paragraph 10).

requirement: Identification and analysis of known and reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety or fundamental rights when used in accordance with the intended purpose.
proposed_control: Impact assessment per system with a harm taxonomy (health, safety, fundamental rights) and affected groups.
notes: Junction with the GDPR DPIA and the fundamental rights impact assessment of Art. 27.

requirement: Estimation and evaluation of risks under intended use and under reasonably foreseeable misuse.
proposed_control: Foreseeable misuse scenarios documented at intake; likelihood and severity matrix.
notes: Recital 65 includes uses outside the instructions that result from easily predictable human behaviour.

requirement: Evaluation of other risks based on data gathered from post-market monitoring.
standard_status: Draft (prEN) / harmonised standard cited in the OJ
proposed_control: Risk register review fed by post-market reports, at a defined cadence.

requirement: Appropriate and targeted risk management measures, with residual risk per hazard and overall judged acceptable: eliminate by design, mitigate what remains, inform and train deployers.
proposed_control: Hierarchy of measures per risk (design, mitigation, information); residual risk acceptance criterion approved by the business owner.
expected_evidence: Risk treatment plan; accepted residual risk statement.
notes: Matches the governance principle: the business owner accepts the risk.

requirement: Testing to identify the most appropriate risk management measures, at any point during development and always before placing on the market, against predefined metrics and probabilistic thresholds.
standards: prEN 18228; ISO 9001:2015 clause 8.3.4 (design and development controls: verification and validation); 8.6 (release)
proposed_control: Test plan with metrics and thresholds fixed before testing; evaluation in CI on every change; results reviewed by a person.
sme_variant: Fixed test set run before every release, with results kept; no mandatory CI pipeline.
expected_evidence: Test plan; threshold reports; CI evaluation history.
notes: Real-world testing only under Art. 60.

requirement: Consideration of adverse impacts on persons under 18 and other vulnerable groups.
proposed_control: Mandatory field in the impact assessment: exposure of minors and vulnerable groups.
expected_evidence: Impact assessment with the field completed.

requirement: Technical documentation drawn up before placing on the market or putting into service, kept up to date, demonstrating compliance with Section 2 and containing at least the elements of Annex IV. SMEs and small mid-caps may use the Commission's simplified form.
standards: EN 18286:2026 (documentation procedures within the QMS); ISO 9001:2015 clause 7.5 (documented information); 8.3.5 (design and development outputs)
standard_status: Harmonised standard cited in the OJ / published standard
proposed_control: Technical documentation template with the Annex IV fields; version linked to each system version.
to_confirm: Whether the simplified form has been published.
notes: The post-market monitoring plan is part of this documentation (Art. 72(3)).

requirement: Systems related to Annex I, Section A products: a single set of technical documentation containing AI Act information and that required by the applicable harmonisation legislation.
proposed_control: Applicable only to regulated products (medical devices, machinery, etc.). Decide applicability.

requirement: Operation sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret and use the output, to the type and degree needed to comply with Section 3.
gdpr: Arts. 13 and 14 (information to data subjects, if applicable)
iso27701: A.1: information to PII principals
proposed_control: Interpretability requirements in the specification (explanations, confidence levels, cited sources).
notes: For source-grounded systems (RAG), a verifiable citation is the practical form of transparency.

requirement: Instructions for use in a digital or other format, concise, complete, correct and clear, with the minimum content of paragraph 3: provider identity; characteristics, capabilities and limitations (intended purpose, accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, risk circumstances, explanatory capabilities, performance per group, input specifications, output interpretation); predetermined changes; human oversight measures; resources and maintenance; logging mechanisms.
standard_status: Draft (prEN) / harmonised standard cited in the OJ
proposed_control: Instructions-for-use template with points (a) to (f) as mandatory sections; review on every version.
expected_evidence: Versioned instructions for use; delivery record to deployers.
notes: As deployer, the organisation should demand these instructions from the vendor and keep them: they are the basis of Art. 26.

requirement: System designed to be effectively overseen by natural persons during use, including through appropriate human-machine interface tools.
proposed_control: Oversight points defined in the specification, proportionate to the system's risk and autonomy.
expected_evidence: Specification with oversight points; acceptance tests.

requirement: Oversight measures built into the system by the provider and/or identified for implementation by the deployer.
proposed_control: Written split of oversight responsibilities between provider and deployer, attached to the instructions for use.
notes: For deployers, this is where human gates before consequential actions belong.

requirement: Overseers can: understand capabilities and limitations and detect anomalies; remain aware of automation bias; correctly interpret output; decide not to use, disregard, override or reverse output; intervene or halt the system safely.
proposed_control: Overseer training (incl. automation bias); stop button and reversal procedure tested; override decisions logged.
sme_variant: Short, recorded training for overseers; stop procedure documented and tested once.
expected_evidence: Training records; stop procedure test; override logs.
notes: Links to Art. 4 (literacy) and Art. 26(2) (deployer assigns oversight to competent persons).

requirement: Remote biometric identification (Annex III, point 1(a)): no action or decision based on the identification unless separately verified by at least two competent persons.
proposed_control: Applicable only if such a system exists. Otherwise mark not applicable with reasons.

requirement: Nominal oversight: the person approves without reviewing because the interface, the volume or the incentives do not allow it (automation bias).
proposed_control: Measure override rate and time per review; secondary review sampling; volume limits per overseer.
notes: Without metrics, effective oversight cannot be shown.

requirement: Appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, performing consistently throughout the lifecycle; accuracy levels and metrics declared in the instructions for use.
proposed_control: Accuracy metrics defined per system with thresholds; drift monitoring; levels published in the instructions.
expected_evidence: Evaluation reports; drift dashboard; instructions for use.
notes: Regression and drift: evaluate on every model or prompt change.

requirement: Resilience to errors, faults and inconsistencies in the system or its environment, through technical and organisational measures including redundancy and fail-safe plans. Systems that continue learning reduce the risk of biased feedback loops.
proposed_control: Explicit, safe failure (no silent errors); retry and cost limits; contingency plan; control of model updates.
expected_evidence: Failure handling design; resilience tests; incident log.
notes: Retry limits and explicit failure are typical existing programme controls.

requirement: Resilience against unauthorised third parties exploiting vulnerabilities to alter use, output or performance; measures against data and model poisoning, adversarial examples, confidentiality attacks and model flaws.
standards: prEN 18282; Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (CRA) where the system is a product with digital elements
proposed_control: Periodic adversarial testing (prompt injection, evasion, extraction); treat external text as data; narrow-scope tools; vulnerability management.
expected_evidence: Red-team reports; vulnerability log; tool configuration.
to_confirm: Articulation with the CRA (the consolidated text lists Reg. 2024/2847 as relevant legislation).
notes: Confirmed in the text: paragraph 5 names data and model poisoning.

requirement: Quality management system documented in written policies, procedures and instructions, covering at least points (a) to (m): compliance strategy and change management; design; development and quality assurance; examination, testing and validation; technical specifications and standards; data management; risk management; post-market monitoring; serious incident reporting; communication with authorities; record keeping; resource management; accountability framework.
standards: EN 18286:2026; ISO 9001:2015 clauses 4 to 10 as generic QMS base (7.5 documented information; 8.3 design and development; 8.5.6 control of changes; 8.7 nonconforming outputs; 9.1 monitoring and measurement; 10.2 corrective action)
standard_status: Harmonised standard cited in the OJ / published standard
proposed_control: Extend the existing management system (ISO 27001 and/or 42001) with the EN 18286 elements rather than build a parallel system.
sme_variant: Proportionate QMS (Art. 17(2)): short policies, no parallel system.
expected_evidence: QMS manual; statement of applicability; EN 18286 ↔ ISO 42001 mapping.
to_confirm: Exact Annex ZA coverage (per one source, points (a) to (m) of paragraph 1, not paragraphs 2 to 4).
notes: The only row where a presumption of conformity is possible: high-risk providers only, and only for what Annex ZA covers.

requirement: Proportionality to the provider's size (SMEs, start-ups, small mid-caps) without lowering the required rigour; integration with sectoral QMS; financial institutions satisfy the obligation through sectoral governance rules except points (g), (h) and (i).
standards: EN 18286:2026; ISO 9001:2015 clause 4.3 (scope) and 8.1 (operational planning), proportionate application
standard_status: Harmonised standard cited in the OJ / published standard
proposed_control: Record organisation size and applicable sectoral legislation at intake to calibrate the QMS.
to_confirm: Whether Annex ZA covers paragraphs 2 to 4.

requirement: Documented, proportionate post-market monitoring system that actively and systematically collects, documents and analyses performance data (from deployers and other sources) to evaluate continuous compliance with Section 2, including interaction with other AI systems.
application_date: Chapter IX: 2 Aug 2026 under Art. 113; in practice operative only once high-risk obligations apply (2 Dec 2027 / 2 Aug 2028)
standards: EN 18286:2026 (post-market processes); ISO 9001:2015 clause 9.1 (monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation); 9.1.2 (customer satisfaction)
standard_status: Harmonised standard cited in the OJ / published standard
proposed_control: Channel to collect data from deployers; periodic analysis of metrics and logs; link to the risk register.
sme_variant: Quarterly review of metrics and logs, minuted.
expected_evidence: Post-market reports; record of data received.
to_confirm: Effective application date (Chapter IX versus high-risk obligations).

requirement: Post-market monitoring plan, part of the Annex IV technical documentation; the Commission adopts guidance and a template by 2 September 2027. Integration with existing plans for Annex I products and financial institutions.
application_date: Chapter IX: 2 Aug 2026 under Art. 113; in practice operative only once high-risk obligations apply (2 Dec 2027 / 2 Aug 2028)
standards: EN 18286:2026; ISO 9001:2015 clause 9.1.1 (planning what to monitor and how)
standard_status: Harmonised standard cited in the OJ / published standard
proposed_control: Plan per system, to be aligned with the Commission template once published.
expected_evidence: Plan annexed to the technical documentation.
to_confirm: Whether the Commission template has been published.
notes: Template deadline amended by the AI Omnibus (Art. 1(30)).

requirement: Serious incident reporting to the market surveillance authority of the Member State where it occurred: immediately after establishing a causal link (or its reasonable likelihood) and at most 15 days after awareness; 2 days for widespread infringements or incidents under Art. 3(49)(b); 10 days in case of death. Initial incomplete report allowed.
application_date: Chapter IX: 2 Aug 2026 under Art. 113; in practice operative only once high-risk obligations apply (2 Dec 2027 / 2 Aug 2028)
standards: EN 18286:2026 (incident reporting procedures); ISO 9001:2015 clause 8.7 (nonconforming outputs); 10.2 (nonconformity and corrective action)
standard_status: Harmonised standard cited in the OJ / published standard
guidance: Commission guidance on serious incidents (due by 2 Aug 2025)
proposed_control: Single incident procedure with a decision tree: AI Act (15/10/2 days), GDPR (72 h), NIS2 or sectoral; authority contacts; initial and full report templates.
sme_variant: One-page procedure with deadlines and contacts; initial report template.
expected_evidence: Procedure; incident log with awareness and reporting dates.
to_confirm: National market surveillance authority; whether the Commission guidance has been published.
notes: The deployer reports to the provider and, under Art. 26(5), may have to report to the authority.

requirement: Investigation without delay after reporting, with risk assessment and corrective measures; cooperation with authorities; no alteration of the system in a way that could affect the evaluation of causes before informing the authorities.
application_date: Chapter IX: 2 Aug 2026 under Art. 113; in practice operative only once high-risk obligations apply (2 Dec 2027 / 2 Aug 2028)
standards: EN 18286:2026; ISO 9001:2015 clause 10.2 (root cause analysis and corrective action)
standard_status: Harmonised standard cited in the OJ / published standard
proposed_control: Evidence preservation (logs, versions) before any fix; root cause analysis; record of corrective measures.
notes: Direct link to Art. 12: without intact logs, no investigation is possible.

requirement: Special regimes: providers subject to equivalent reporting obligations under other Union law limit reporting to incidents under Art. 3(49)(c); medical devices likewise, to the designated national authority.
application_date: Chapter IX: 2 Aug 2026 under Art. 113; in practice operative only once high-risk obligations apply (2 Dec 2027 / 2 Aug 2028)
proposed_control: Map the reporting regimes the provider is already subject to before designing the procedure.

requirement: Measures to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy of staff and others operating AI systems on the organisation's behalf, taking into account their knowledge, experience, training, context and the persons affected. Does not require guaranteeing any specific literacy level.
iso27701: Clause 7.2 / 7.3: competence and awareness on PII protection
proposed_control: Training programme per profile (user, approver, overseer, developer), with attendance and content records; periodic renewal.
sme_variant: Mandatory initial session and reference material; record of completion.
expected_evidence: Training plan; attendance records; versioned content.
to_confirm: Whether the Commission has published the practical examples.
notes: The AI Omnibus softened the wording: an obligation of means, not of result.

requirement: Do not place on the market, put into service or use systems that: use subliminal, manipulative or deceptive techniques distorting behaviour with significant harm (a); exploit vulnerabilities of age, disability or socio-economic situation (b); perform social scoring (c); predict criminal offences from profiling alone (d); build facial recognition databases by untargeted scraping (e); infer emotions in the workplace or education, except for medical or safety reasons (f); perform biometric categorisation to infer race, political opinions, trade union membership, beliefs, sex life or sexual orientation (g); real-time remote biometric identification for law enforcement outside the exceptions (h).
iso27701: A.1: legal basis; PII principals' rights (profiling limits)
proposed_control: Prohibited practices list as a blocking criterion at intake: a 'yes' on any ends the assessment. Special attention to HR tools inferring emotions or mood.
expected_evidence: Intake checklist with the prohibited practices section; record of refused cases.
notes: A prohibited practice is not a risk decision: it leaves the flow. Point (f) is the most likely in an ordinary organisation (employee sentiment analysis, meeting monitoring).

requirement: Do not place on the market, put into service or use systems that generate or manipulate intimate or sexually explicit images, video or audio of identifiable persons without explicit consent (ba), or child sexual abuse material (bb); for providers, prohibited only if it is the intended purpose or a foreseeable, reproducible result without safeguards; for deployers, if used for that purpose.
ai_act_basis: Art. 5(1)(ba) and (bb); (1a) and (1b) (introduced by the AI Omnibus)
proposed_control: Acceptable use policy expressly prohibiting this use; content filters on approved tools; reporting channel.
sme_variant: Clause in the acceptable use policy.
expected_evidence: Signed policy; filter configuration; incident log.
notes: AI Omnibus novelty. For pure deployers, the obligation reduces to not using tools for this purpose and being able to detect it.

requirement: Classify each system: high-risk if it is a safety component of an Annex I product subject to third-party conformity assessment (para 1), or listed in Annex III (para 2). Systems used solely for user assistance, optimisation, efficiency, automation, convenience or quality control are not safety components, unless failure could endanger health and safety (paras 1a and 1b).
ai_act_basis: Art. 6(1) to (2); Annex I; Annex III
application_date: Chapter III, Section 1: 2 Dec 2027 / 2 Aug 2028; classification needed now for planning
guidance: Draft Commission guidelines on Art. 6 (published 19 May 2026; consultation closed 23 Jun 2026; final adoption not verified)
proposed_control: Classification step at triage, with the eight Annex III areas as a closed list and the safety-component question. Result recorded in the use-case register.
expected_evidence: Use-case register with classification and reasoning.
to_confirm: Final adoption of the Art. 6 guidelines (draft of 19 May 2026).
notes: Most likely Annex III areas in an ordinary organisation: point 4 (recruitment, employment decisions, performance evaluation) and point 5(b) (credit) and (c) (insurance). Point 8 (justice) targets judicial authorities.

requirement: Derogation: an Annex III system is not high-risk if it poses no significant risk and does not materially influence the outcome: narrow procedural task; improving a completed human activity; detecting decision patterns or deviations without replacing human assessment; preparatory task. Never applies if the system profiles natural persons.
proposed_control: Test of the four conditions at triage, with automatic exclusion where profiling is involved.
expected_evidence: Derogation reasoning in the use-case register.
notes: For deployers, the derogation is invoked by the provider (para 4); ask them for the documented assessment.

requirement: A provider considering an Annex III system not high-risk documents the assessment before placing it on the market, registers the system (Art. 49(2)) and provides the documentation to authorities on request.
proposed_control: Derogation assessment template; registration in the EU database.

requirement: Technical and organisational measures to use the system in accordance with the instructions for use.
standards: ISO 9001:2015 clause 8.4 (control of externally provided processes, products and services)
proposed_control: Keep each system's instructions for use; translate restrictions into configuration and usage rules; check at periodic review.
sme_variant: Per-system sheet with the restrictions from the instructions and who checks them.
expected_evidence: Archived instructions; documented configuration; review minutes.
notes: An approved-tool sheet is the natural home for this.

requirement: Human oversight assigned to persons with the necessary competence, training, authority and support.
proposed_control: Formal appointment of overseers per system, with recorded training and authority to suspend use.
notes: Links to R-14.03 (what the overseer must be able to do) and R-04.01 (literacy).

requirement: To the extent the deployer controls input data, ensure it is relevant and sufficiently representative for the intended purpose.
proposed_control: Specify which data enter each system and check their quality and coverage before use.

requirement: Inform workers' representatives and affected workers before putting into service or using a high-risk system in the workplace, under applicable labour law.
proposed_control: Prior information procedure for workers and representatives, aligned with labour law and GDPR information.
to_confirm: Applicable national rules on worker information and consultation.
notes: Relevant for HR and performance monitoring tools.

requirement: Use the information received from the provider (Art. 13) to carry out the data protection impact assessment (Art. 35 GDPR).
iso27701: A.1: privacy impact assessment
proposed_control: DPIA template with a section incorporating the instructions for use and the provider's declared limitations.
expected_evidence: DPIA with the provider's instructions annexed.
notes: With Art. 27(4), closes the single intake feeding both assessments.

requirement: Deployers that are public authorities or Union bodies register the system (Art. 49) and do not use high-risk systems not registered in the EU database.
proposed_control: Check of EU database registration before use.

requirement: Fundamental rights impact assessment before first use of an Annex III high-risk system (except point 2), by bodies governed by public law, private entities providing public services, and deployers of credit scoring and insurance systems (Annex III, point 5(b) and (c)). Content: processes, period and frequency, affected persons and groups, specific risks of harm, human oversight, measures and complaint mechanisms.
iso27701: A.1: privacy impact assessment (shared method)
proposed_control: Assessment template with the six points, shared with the DPIA; review when any element changes.
to_confirm: Whether the AI Office template has been published.
notes: Applies only to the subjects in paragraph 1; an ordinary private company is in scope only if it provides public services or assesses credit or insurance.

requirement: Notify the market surveillance authority of the results, submitting the completed template; may refer to or integrate parts of the DPIA.
proposed_control: Notification step in the procedure, with explicit references to reused DPIA sections.

requirement: Systems interacting directly with persons inform them they are interacting with AI, unless obvious to a reasonably informed person.
proposed_control: Clear notice at first interaction; route to a human.
notes: Deployers of third-party chatbots should check the notice exists and not remove it.

requirement: Systems generating synthetic content (audio, image, video, text) mark outputs in a machine-readable, detectable format, with effective and interoperable solutions as far as technically feasible; exceptions for standard editing assistance and non-substantial alterations.
application_date: Since 2 Aug 2026; systems placed on the market before that date: by 2 Dec 2026
proposed_control: Marking (metadata, watermark) in own systems; in third-party tools, check that marking exists and do not disable it.
expected_evidence: Marking specification; verification on approved tools.
to_confirm: Status of the codes of practice on marking.
notes: Transitional period introduced by the AI Omnibus (Art. 111(4)).

requirement: Deployers of emotion recognition or biometric categorisation systems inform exposed persons and process data under the GDPR.
iso27701: A.1: information to PII principals; A.1: consent
proposed_control: Prior notice to exposed persons; legal basis for biometric data documented.
notes: In the workplace and education, emotion recognition is prohibited (Art. 5(1)(f)): this row applies only outside those contexts.

requirement: Deployers disclose generated or manipulated content: deep fakes of image, audio or video (lighter regime for artistic works); text published to inform the public on matters of public interest, unless under human review or editorial control with an editorially responsible person.
proposed_control: Rule in the acceptable use policy: externally published generated content passes human review with an editorial owner, or carries an AI-generated notice.
notes: Relevant for articles, newsletters and marketing content produced with AI.

requirement: Legal basis for each AI processing operation (training, fine-tuning, inference) and purpose compatibility where data collected for another purpose are reused.
iso27701: A.1: purpose identification; legal basis; consent; records of processing
guidance: EDPB Opinion 28/2024 (legitimate interest in training; model anonymity)
proposed_control: Mandatory intake field: legal basis per operation and compatibility test where data are reused.
notes: The EDPB treats legitimate interest as a possible basis for training, subject to the three-step test.

requirement: Information to data subjects about AI processing, including the existence of automated decisions and the logic involved.
iso27701: A.1: information to PII principals (privacy notice; automated decision-making)
proposed_control: Update privacy policies and collection notices with AI use and, where present, automated decisions.

requirement: Solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects: prohibited unless contract, law or explicit consent; right to human intervention, to express one's view and to contest; limits with special categories.
iso27701: A.1: PII principals' rights (automated decision-making; human review)
guidance: Article 29 WP guidelines on automated decision-making (WP251)
proposed_control: Triage criterion 'suggests or acts': any system deciding alone with effects on people requires real human review or a documented exception.
expected_evidence: Triage with the criterion; human intervention procedure.
notes: Nominal oversight (RK-14.A) does not satisfy Art. 22.

requirement: Data protection by design and by default; minimisation in prompts, logs and training data.
iso27701: A.1: privacy by design and by default; data minimisation; A.3: pseudonymisation
proposed_control: Data classification rule by system type; pseudonymisation before sending to vendors; retention and training disabled at vendors.

requirement: AI vendors processing personal data on the organisation's behalf are processors: contract with the Art. 28(3) clauses, including instructions, confidentiality, security, sub-processing, deletion and audit.
iso27701: A.1: PII processor engagement and contracts; A.2: customer agreement; subcontractor disclosure
proposed_control: Vendor assessment checking the data processing agreement, the sub-processor list and the no-training clause.

requirement: Security of processing appropriate to the risk, including pseudonymisation, confidentiality, integrity, availability and regular testing.
iso27701: A.3: information security controls for PII (29 selected controls)
proposed_control: Access control and least privilege in AI integrations; user identity carried through calls; periodic security testing.
notes: Narrow-scope tools and least privilege are typical existing programme controls.

requirement: Notification of personal data breaches to the authority within 72 hours and, where the risk is high, to data subjects.
iso27701: A.1 / A.2: PII breach notification to authorities, principals and customers
proposed_control: The same incident procedure as R-73.01, with the GDPR decision tree: breach, risk, 72-hour deadline, communication to data subjects.
notes: Leaks through prompts or unapproved AI tools are data breaches like any other.

requirement: Data protection impact assessment where processing is likely to result in high risk, notably systematic evaluation by automated processing, large-scale special categories or systematic monitoring; prior consultation of the authority if residual risk remains high.
iso27701: A.1: privacy impact assessment
guidance: National supervisory authority's list of processing requiring a DPIA
proposed_control: Single intake feeding the DPIA and, where applicable, the fundamental rights impact assessment; trigger criterion at triage.
expected_evidence: DPIA per system; reasoned decision not to perform a DPIA.

requirement: Record of processing activities updated with AI processing, including the Art. 4a reasons where applicable.
iso27701: A.1: records of PII processing
proposed_control: The use-case register feeds the record of processing activities, with a linking field between the two.

requirement: International transfers of personal data to AI vendors outside the EEA: adequacy decision, standard contractual clauses or another mechanism, with a transfer impact assessment.
iso27701: A.1 / A.2: international transfer of PII; countries and organisations to which PII can be transferred
proposed_control: Data and sub-processor location checked in the vendor assessment; transfer mechanism recorded.
expected_evidence: Vendor assessment with the transfer mechanism.
to_confirm: EU-US DPF: upheld by the General Court (3 Sep 2025), appeal pending before the CJEU; UK adequacy renewal not verified.

requirement: Special categories of data in AI systems only under one of the Art. 9(2) exceptions and, where the purpose is bias correction, with the Art. 4a AI Act safeguards.
iso27701: A.1: legal basis for special categories; A.3: access control
proposed_control: Block at intake: special categories only with an identified exception and DPO consulted.
notes: Links to R-10.11 and R-10.12.

requirement: Hallucination: the system produces plausible but false statements, citations or references that reach a client, a court or a decision.
guidance: NIST AI RMF — Generative AI Profile; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
proposed_control: Source grounding and programmatic citation checking; rule that nothing generated leaves without human review by a named owner; hallucination-rate evaluation in CI.
sme_variant: Mandatory human review rule and an approved tool list with source citation.
expected_evidence: Citation check results; review record; evaluation metrics.

requirement: Prompt injection: untrusted text (documents, emails, web pages, tool outputs) enters the model context and alters instructions or exfiltrates data.
proposed_control: Treat external content as data, not instructions; restrict the tools available to the agent; human approval before consequential actions; periodic adversarial testing.
sme_variant: On third-party tools: do not connect the model to external sources without need; do not give the agent the ability to act.
expected_evidence: Tool design; adversarial test reports; approval log.

requirement: Excessive permissions: agents and integrations with more access than the task requires, or acting with shared credentials instead of the user's identity.
proposed_control: Least privilege per tool; user identity carried through; approval thresholds by value or impact; periodic access review.
expected_evidence: Permission matrix per agent; access review record.

requirement: Content safety: harmful, discriminatory or safeguard-bypassing responses reaching people outside the organisation.
guidance: NIST AI RMF — Generative AI Profile
proposed_control: Layers: input and output filters, adversarial testing, measurement of harm rate and of wrongful refusal rate, user reporting channel.
sme_variant: Use only approved tools with vendor filters; internal reporting channel.

requirement: Systems used as safety components in the management and operation of critical digital infrastructure, road traffic and the supply of water, gas, heating and electricity are high-risk (Annex III, point 2). Network automation counts only if failure could endanger health and safety (Art. 6(1a) and (1b)).
proposed_control: At triage, for each network automation or optimisation system, document whether it is a safety component: what happens if it fails.
notes: Art. 27 excludes Annex III point 2 from the fundamental rights impact assessment.

requirement: Essential and important entities adopt proportionate cybersecurity risk management measures, including supply chain security, security in system acquisition and development, incident handling and continuity; AI systems and their vendors fall within scope.
application_date: Directive: 18 Oct 2024; Portugal: Decree-Law 125/2025, in force 3 Apr 2026
proposed_control: Include AI systems in the asset inventory and the NIS2 risk analysis; assess AI vendors against supply chain criteria.
expected_evidence: Risk analysis covering AI systems; vendor assessments.
to_confirm: Transposition status in Member States other than Portugal.
notes: Directive (EU) 2022/2555, Art. 21. Applies to telecoms, energy, transport, health, banking, digital infrastructure and others.

requirement: Significant incident notification to the CSIRT or authority: early warning within 24 hours, notification within 72 hours, final report within one month.
application_date: Directive: 18 Oct 2024; Portugal: Decree-Law 125/2025, in force 3 Apr 2026
proposed_control: Single incident decision tree across the three regimes: NIS2 (24 h / 72 h / 1 month), GDPR (72 h) and AI Act (15 / 10 / 2 days).
to_confirm: Deadlines in Member States other than Portugal.
notes: Directive (EU) 2022/2555, Art. 23. Portugal (Decree-Law 125/2025): alert within 24 h, update within 72 h, end-of-impact notice, final report within 30 business days, to the CNCS.

requirement: Financial entities maintain an ICT risk management framework covering AI systems; ICT third-party risk, including AI vendors, is managed with a register of information, pre-contractual assessment and mandatory contractual clauses.
guidance: ESAs regulatory technical standards under DORA
proposed_control: Integrate AI systems into the ICT risk framework and the third-party register of information; check whether the AI vendor is a critical provider.
expected_evidence: Register of information; vendor assessment; contract with the DORA Art. 30 clauses.
notes: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, Arts. 5 to 16 and 28 to 30. The AI Act refers to these rules in Art. 17(4) and Art. 26(5).

requirement: Reporting of major ICT-related incidents to the competent authority: initial notification within 4 hours of classification as major and no later than 24 hours from awareness; intermediate report within 72 hours of the initial notification; final report within one month of the latest intermediate report (RTS 2025/301).
ai_act_basis: Art. 73(9) (limited reporting where an equivalent regime exists)
proposed_control: Include AI system incidents in the DORA procedure; check whether Art. 73(9) limits AI Act reporting to Art. 3(49)(c) incidents.
notes: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, Art. 19; Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/301 (time limits and content). Classification criteria: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772.

requirement: Systems evaluating creditworthiness or credit scores of natural persons (except fraud detection) and risk assessment and pricing in life and health insurance are high-risk.
proposed_control: Inventory credit and insurance pricing models and classify them; for deployers, prepare the fundamental rights impact assessment (R-27.01).
notes: The 'fria' profile question activates Art. 27 for these systems.

requirement: AI software that is a medical device or a safety component of a device subject to third-party conformity assessment is high-risk under Annex I; technical documentation is single and incident reporting is limited to Art. 3(49)(c), to the designated national authority.
guidance: MDCG guidance on software and AI
proposed_control: Integrate AI Act requirements into the MDR quality management system (ISO 13485) rather than build a parallel one.
notes: Regulations (EU) 2017/745 and 2017/746.

requirement: Professional secrecy and confidentiality in AI tools: client data only in approved tools, with no vendor retention or training, isolated per client and per matter.
iso27701: A.2: processing on customer instructions; confidentiality; A.3: access control
guidance: Professional body guidance on AI (to confirm)
proposed_control: Data classification rule by system type; approved tool list with no-training and no-retention clauses; conflict-of-interest controls on context sharing across matters.
expected_evidence: Approved tool list; vendor terms; classification rule.
to_confirm: Applicable professional conduct rules on AI use.
notes: Annex III, point 8(a) targets judicial authorities or those acting on their behalf; lawyer support tools do not enter by that route unless used on behalf of a court.

requirement: Connected products and related services: generated data must be accessible to the user and, at the user's request, to third parties, with pre-contractual information on the data generated; data obtained may not be used to develop competing products.
application_date: Since 12 Sep 2025 (access-by-design for products placed on the market after 12 Sep 2026)
proposed_control: If the organisation makes connected products or trains models on their data, map which data are 'product data' and ensure access and use restrictions.
notes: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854, Arts. 3 to 7; dates confirmed against Art. 50.

requirement: Switching between data processing (cloud) service providers: contracts must allow switching and data portability within defined periods, with switching charges phased out.
application_date: Since 12 Sep 2025 (switching charges abolished from 12 Jan 2027)
proposed_control: In cloud AI vendor assessments, check switching and portability clauses; avoid dependence on proprietary formats for data and prompts.
expected_evidence: Contractual clauses; exit plan per vendor.
notes: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854, Arts. 23 to 31 (switching charges: Art. 29); dates confirmed against Art. 50. Relevant for anyone dependent on a single model provider.

requirement: Products with digital elements meet the essential cybersecurity and vulnerability handling requirements of Annex I, with conformity assessment and CE marking; high-risk AI software meeting the CRA is presumed to comply with Art. 15 AI Act for what the CRA covers.
ai_act_basis: Art. 42(3) (inserted by the AI Omnibus); CRA Art. 12
proposed_control: Classify the product under the CRA (default, important, critical); integrate vulnerability handling into the AI system lifecycle.
expected_evidence: CRA conformity assessment; vulnerability disclosure policy.
notes: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847. Confirmed in the official Omnibus text: new Art. 42(3) AI Act deems CRA-compliant high-risk systems to meet Art. 15 where CRA Art. 12(1) conditions are fulfilled. Commission CRA guidance published 27 Jul 2026.

requirement: Reporting of actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents affecting product security: early warning within 24 hours, notification within 72 hours, final report within 14 days (vulnerabilities) or one month (incidents), through the single reporting platform.
proposed_control: Include the CRA in the incident decision tree, alongside the AI Act, the GDPR and NIS2.
notes: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847, Art. 14; applies since 11 Sep 2026 to all in-scope products already on the market (Art. 69(3)); ENISA Single Reporting Platform.

requirement: Recruitment and selection systems (targeted job ads, application screening, candidate evaluation) and systems for decisions affecting the employment relationship (promotion, termination, task allocation based on behaviour or traits, monitoring and performance evaluation) are high-risk.
proposed_control: Inventory HR tools with AI (including AI modules in software already licensed) and classify them; apply R-26.04 (worker information) and check they do not infer emotions (R-05.01).
notes: The most likely high-risk case in any organisation, because it arrives through HR software nobody chose as an 'AI system'.
